newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia-EU demand immediate release of Peru hostages.
newsitem.headline: Asia-EU demand immediate release of Peru hostages.

text.p: Asian and European foreign ministers on Saturday demanded the immediate release of all hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru.
Twenty five ministers meeting in Singapore said in a statement they strongly condemned the "criminal act" and reaffirmed their determination not to give in to terrorism.
The Lima hostage crisis erupted on December 27 when a band of heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement rebels stormed a cocktail party at the residence and seized hundreds of guests.
All but 72 mostly middle-aged VIP men have been released.

"They (the foreign ministers) expressed their solidarity with the governments of Peru and Japan and supported the efforts of both governments to resolve the situation in a peaceful manner, with the priority of saving lives of all hostages," the statement said.

The Singapore meeting was attended by ministers from the 15-member European Union, those from the Association of Southeast Nations -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam -- plus China, South Korea and Japan.
The ministers welcomed the start of preliminary dialogue between the interlocutor of the Peruvian government and the rebel representatives, it said.
The Peruvian government and the Marxist rebels were due to meet again on Saturday to try to draft an agenda for talks to end the crisis peacefully.
Crisis mediators have said the two sides made "real progress" on Friday when they swapped lists of items they want on the agenda.
